projectDescription: Designing a “revival typeface” based on a previously undigitized font.
prompts: Scanning images of old type specimens at a physical archive
Sharing a beta version of the font with designer friends to test
Surveying current type foundries online for similar typefaces
Exploring online archives for inspiration
Reading Designing Type Revivals to decide how much of the original ink-on-paper artifact to carry into the digital version
Watching tutorials on specific features in Glyphs
Asking an AI agent about the history of the original typeface, its foundry, and its designer
Meeting with instructor and/or archivist to find examples of the original typeface in use

projectDescription: Working with a news outlet to improve the user experience of their digital product
prompts: Shadowing an editor through a morning production cycle in the newsroom
Sharing a clickable prototype with regular readers to test
Surveying how other newspapers online handle paywalls and subscription flows
Exploring online archives of the paper's past print and web redesigns for inspiration
Reading The Elements of User Experience to decide how much of the print edition's hierarchy to carry into the digital version
Watching tutorials on specific features in Figma
Searching the web about the history of the newspaper, its ownership, and its editorial position
Conducting workshops with readers to see how they move through the current site
Conducting workshops with readers to see how they  move through the redesigned site

projectDescription: Designing wall graphics and a monograph for a group exhibition at a contemporary art museum
prompts: Visiting the empty gallery to measure walls, sightlines, and lighting
Mocking up vinyl lettering at full scale in the studio to test legibility from across a room
Meeting with curator about the sequence of rooms and what a visitor should notice first
Building a scale mockup of the gallery space
Doing suggested readings provided by artists to help conceptualize relationship between work and gallery
Collecting catalogues from comparable shows to study how essays, plates, and checklists are ordered
Meeting with the fabricator to understand cutting constraints and installation tolerances
Visiting the printer to check capabilityies and compare paper stocks/binding options
Reading interviews, reviews and critiques of artists' works

projectDescription: Designing an interactive data visualization for a national news outlet about an ongoing economic and geopolitical crisis
prompts: Tracing a dataset back to the agency that produced it to learn what its categories count and exclude
Searching web to explain indicators in play and how economists disagree about what they measure
Collecting examples of compelling interactive visualizations on are.na
Sketching the piece on paper first to decide what the reader should be able to do, not just see
Prototyping initial visualization in Datawrapper to test legibility
Reading on the politics of quantification to decide what a single figure is being asked to stand in for
Testing the piece with readers outside the newsroom to see what they conclude without being told
Reviewing how other outlets have visualized the same crisis, and where their framing became an argument
Testing near-complete form across multiple browsers and systems to ensure maximum compatibility

projectDescription: Developing a new identity system for a non-profit which focuses on cycling and urban space in Toronto
prompts: Riding around the city and photographing the signage and street conditions along the way
Interviewing staff and volunteers about who they are trying to persuade — riders, drivers, or councillors
Auditing the organization's existing materials to see which marks people actually recognize
Comparing the identities of transit agencies, municipal wayfinding, and other advocacy groups working on the same topic in different cities
Reading on the politics of street space to decide whether the identity should read as civic or oppositional
Testing marks at the sizes they'll actually appear — a jersey, a lawn sign, a bike frame decal, a petition header
Reviewing historic and contemproary brand guideline manuals for inspiration

projectDescription: Collecting materials and developing a web-archive of design ephemera related to the mid-90s DIY screamo
prompts: Photographing show flyers, 7" sleeves, and zines from a collector's basement
Emailing people who ran labels and distros to ask what they still have and whether it can be scanned
Looking at collected materials to determine categories, time ranges, and regions to use as dynamic content filters
Reading on the politics of the archive to decide who has standing to consent to any of this being public
Surveying existing web-archives of subcultural material to see what their metadata schemas assume
Testing the site's browse structure with people from the scene to see whether the categories match how they remember it
Asking AI about which Content Management System is best to effectively run the database for the archived materials

projectDescription: Writing an article about the history of early interface design
prompts: Reading the original technical reports and manuals rather than the histories written about them
Watching archived the demo footage and screen recordings that survive, and noting what didn't get recorded
Emulating the software to see how it actually behaved, rather than describing it from screenshots
Reading on the historiography of technology to decide whether to write invention or accumulation
Tracing who the standard account credits and who was doing the work it credits them for
Deciding what images the argument requires, and whether they can be reproduced
Reading other articles in the proposed publication to get a sense of the writing style
Interviewing older computer users to get a sense of the usage and problems of various interfaces

projectDescription: Working with a citizen science organization to develop a user-friendly "DIY Water Quality Monitoring Kit"
prompts: Running the existing testing protocol yourself, at a real site, to find where it breaks down
Interviewing volunteers about what they gave up on and why they stopped submitting readings
Researching the parameters being measured and what a reading can and cannot establish
Meeting with the organization's scientists to learn which steps are negotiable and which invalidate the data
Prototyping the instruction sheet in the field, wet-handed, in bad light
Reading on the politics of environmental evidence to decide who this data has to convince
Sourcing and pricing components to see what the kit costs at fifty units versus five hundred
Testing the kit with someone who has never done this before, and watching without helping

projectDescription: Working with an illustrator to art direct spot illustrations for a cover story in The Walrus
prompts: Reading the piece to understand its argument/narrative clearly
Reading on the relationship between text and image to decide whether the spots illustrate, interrupt, or argue
Meeting with the editor to learn what the story can't be seen to be saying
Building a reference deck of illustrators whose work would suit the tone and subject matter of the article
Writing the brief so it names a problem to solve rather than a picture to make
Mapping where the spots fall against the page grid and the flow of the text
Giving feedback on sketches in terms of the story's beats

projectDescription: Working with a local politician to develop an ongoing series of social media videos profiling bylaws and civic services
prompts: Reading on public communication and propaganda to decide where explaining ends and campaigning begins
Reading the actual bylaw text to see how much of it survives translation into ninety seconds
Meeting with the councillor's staff to learn what they can say in an official capacity and what they can't
Asking an AI agent how the service is structured and which level of government is actually responsible
Shadowing a city worker delivering the service, and shooting reference footage while there
Studying how other municipal accounts handle vertical video, captions, and sound-off viewing
Building a title, caption, and lower-third system that holds up across fifty episodes made by different hands
Testing a cut with residents who have never contacted the city, and seeing whether they understand what to do next
